faq.question: Do Belgian Shopify stores usually need both Dutch and French as real storefront languages?
faq.answer: Often yes, especially when Belgium is more than a side market. If Dutch and French both matter for discovery, trust, and conversion, treating one as primary and the other as a thin fallback usually leaves part of the same-country customer journey under-served.

faq.question: When does German in Belgium deserve more than a narrow fallback layer?
faq.answer: German deserves more than symbolic coverage when there is real traffic, support demand, regional commercial importance, or a policy reason strong enough to justify a meaningful storefront path. Without that evidence, it is often better to keep German narrowly scoped than to launch a weak full layer.

faq.question: What breaks when Dutch and French do not ship with release parity?
faq.answer: When one language updates faster than the other, metadata drifts, product coverage becomes uneven, and shipping, returns, or support pages start falling back into the wrong language. That is usually when a Belgian storefront stops feeling intentionally multilingual and starts feeling unreliable.
